verdicts.evidence: Unauthenticated `curl https://fbc-api.recycleservers.com/v1/workers` (no CF-Access headers) at 2026-10-31T20:2xZ -> HTTP/2 401 {"detail":"Missing bearer token"}, a FastAPI origin body. Cloudflare Access would have answered with a 302 to *.cloudflareaccess.com or a 403 at the edge. `GET /` -> 200 serving the Fleet console HTML; `GET /openapi.json` -> 200, so the whole endpoint map (relogin included) is public. The docs claim Access in apps/backend/src/routes/coordinator.ts:37-38 and trackers/facebook/AGENTS.md:43.
verdicts.reason: Reproduced: the edge lets anonymous traffic through to rs_console, and the bearer token is the only factor. The failure scenario overstates one point: COORDINATOR_API_TOKEN/RS_CONSOLE_TOKEN was rotated on 2026-10-22 after the Railway disclosure, so the token that leaked no longer works. The missing second factor and the public console UI and OpenAPI are still real. P2 stands because no current credential is known to be exposed.

verdicts.evidence: Cloudflare API GET r2/buckets/recycle-erp-attachments/cors (repro/B2-verify/attachments-cors.json) has one rule whose origins are only https://inventory.recycleservers.com. infra/terraform/environments/prod/main.tf:32-36 declares 3 origins. Live probe (repro/B2-verify/attachments-cors-probe.txt): a GET for a real image on static.recycleservers.com with Origin inventory.recycleservers.com returns Access-Control-Allow-Origin, and with Origin inventory-prod or inventory-dev it returns 200 with no ACAO header. inventory-prod is a declared prod route in deploy/cloudflare/wrangler.toml:53. photoSourceFile() (apps/frontend/src/lib/linePhotos.ts:283-295) does a plain cross-origin fetch and returns null when the fetch fails.
verdicts.reason: Reproduced against the live bucket. The Terraform change was never applied, so the INF-02 fix that was checked off does not exist in production. It hits only users on the secondary hostname, which keeps it at P2.

verdicts.evidence: Cloudflare API: r2/buckets/recycle-db-backup/lock -> {"rules":[]} (repro/B2-verify/backup-lock.json); lifecycle has only 'Default Multipart Abort Rule' (backup-lifecycle.json). backup/backup.sh:102-111 runs `rclone deletefile` with the same R2 credential that uploads. Memory note railway-security-disclosure-2026-10-21 lists 'R2 x3' rotation as pending as of 2026-10-23.
verdicts.reason: No retention lock, and the writer can delete: both confirmed. Correction: R2 has no object versioning feature, so 'no versioning' is not a missing setting. The fix is a bucket lock rule with an Age retention of at least BACKUP_KEEP days (or a separate prune credential). I did not verify whether the R2 rotation is still pending after 2026-10-23: that needs token ages from the owner. P2 is appropriate; exploiting it needs a compromised credential plus loss of the Railway DB.

needs_owner: Confirm whether the R2 API tokens (backup writer included) were rotated after 2026-10-23; I can't check token age read-only without the dashboard.

Decide whether fbc-api.recycleservers.com should get a Cloudflare Access application (service-token policy) to match the documented contract. The ERP already sends COORDINATOR_ACCESS_CLIENT_* headers.
